newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt, EU might agree in principle on trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt, EU might agree in principle on trade.

text.p: Egypt said on Thursday it might yet reach a framework trade agreement with the European Union (EU) in time for a meeting of European and Mediterranean foreign ministers in Malta next month.

But Gamal Bayyoumi, Egypt's chief negotiator in talks on an association agreement with the EU, told reporters the European side needs to be more flexible in the talks, held up by disputes over the quotas for Egypt's agricultural exports to Europe.

Bayyoumi headed a round of talks in Cairo earlier this month and Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo, whose country now holds the EU presidency, is expected in Cairo for more talks between now and the Malta meeting on April 15/16.

"With more cooperation and flexibility from the European side, and with the Egyptian side ready to make every effort, the gap between the two sides will be bridged and they will be able...in Malta to announce they have reached an agreeement on basic principles governing an association agreement," he said.
Bayyoumi was speaking after briefing European ambassadors on details of the last round of talks. He said the talks had now reached "a very good stage".

The association agreement, similar to those the EU has signed with Morocco and Tunisia, will bring in free trade in manufactured goods and services but not in farm produce -- the area where Egypt has the most promising short-term opportunities.
